title: The git commands you'll type
summary: status, add, commit and switch, one at a time on the board.

steps.title: Four commands
steps.say: Most days you only need four git commands. Let's go through them one at a time.

board.code:
git status
git add roster.txt
git commit -m "Add my name to the roster"
git switch -c issue-12-add-turbo-boost

steps.title: status
steps.say: **What's changed?** Run it whenever you're unsure. It lists changed files and tells you which branch you're on.

board.code:
git status
git add roster.txt
git commit -m "Add my name to the roster"
git switch -c issue-12-add-turbo-boost

marks.label: what changed, and which branch am I on?

steps.title: add
steps.say: **Stage** a file: put it in the next snapshot. You choose what goes in, so half-finished work can wait.

board.code:
git status
git add roster.txt
git commit -m "Add my name to the roster"
git switch -c issue-12-add-turbo-boost

marks.label: what changed, and which branch am I on?
put this file in the next commit

steps.title: commit
steps.say: **Save the snapshot** with a message. `-m` means "here's the message". Write it for a teammate reading the history next month.

board.code:
git status
git add roster.txt
git commit -m "Add my name to the roster"
git switch -c issue-12-add-turbo-boost

marks.label: what changed, and which branch am I on?
put this file in the next commit
save a snapshot of what's staged
the message: what changed and why

steps.title: switch
steps.say: **Move to another branch.** `-c` creates it first. New work goes on a feature branch off `develop`, never straight onto `main`.

board.code:
git status
git add roster.txt
git commit -m "Add my name to the roster"
git switch -c issue-12-add-turbo-boost

marks.label: what changed, and which branch am I on?
put this file in the next commit
save a snapshot of what's staged
the message: what changed and why
make a new branch and move onto it

steps.title: Bringing work together
steps.say: When a feature is done, you **merge** it into `develop`. If two branches changed the same line, git stops and asks you to choose. That's a merge conflict, and the git lesson walks you through one.

board.code:
git switch develop
git merge issue-12-add-turbo-boost

marks.label: go to the branch you're merging into
bring the feature branch's commits in
